Question: A merchant buys a number of oranges at \(3\) for \(10\)¢ and an equal number at \(5\) for \(20\)¢. To “break even” he must sell all at:
Solution:
To break even, the merchant must recover his total purchase cost. Use equal batches of \(15\) oranges for the calculation, since \(15\) is divisible by both \(3\) and \(5\). Scaling both purchases by the same factor scales total cost and total quantity together, so it leaves the required selling rate unchanged.

The first batch costs \(5\cdot10=50\) cents, and the second costs \(3\cdot20=60\) cents. Thus \(30\) oranges cost \(110\) cents. These oranges make \(10\) groups of \(3\), so each group must sell for
\[
\frac{110}{10}=11\text{ cents}.
\]
He must sell at \(\boxed{3\text{ for }11\text{¢}}\), choice B.
